 Order
This Writ Petition has been filed challenging the order passed by the fourth respondent dated 24.08.2018, thereby, imposed fine of Rs.1,00,000/- payable by the petitioner.

2. Heard the learned counsel on either side and perused the materials available on record.
3.
The petitioner is the Proprietor of Dindigul Kumaran Sambar powder, having unit at Dindigul.
The distributors used to purchase the said product and distribute the same in their respective areas.
While being so, on 23.02.2017, the third respondent inspected and lifted sample from his shop.
It was sent tot he Food Analysis test.

The food analysis https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis report dated 24.03.2017, opined that the sample is mis-branded under Section 3(1)(zf) (c) (I) of the Food Safety and Standards Act (hereinafter referred as the Act).
On receipt of the said report, the third respondent filed a charge sheet for adjudication by the fourth respondent.
The petitioner was served with notice dated 06.11.2017, thereby directed the petitioner to appear before the fourth respondent for adjudication on 17.11.2017.
Thereafter, the petitioner requested the adjudication authority to serve copy of the complaint and connected document to defend the case.

However, without furnishing any copy of the complaint and the other document,
the fourth respondent/ adjudicating authority passed the order dated 24.08.2018, thereby, imposed a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- payable by the petitioner.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that during the adjudication proceedings, the fourth respondent ought to have served notice by giving 30 days time to appear before the adjudicating authority as contemplated under Section 3.1.1.(6) of the Food Safety and Standards https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Rules, 2011.
It should annexed the analysis report as contemplated under the Rules.
Further the petitioner submitted a representation asking for the copy of the charge sheet and other annexed documents.
However, the petitioner was not provided with any of the documents and mechanically passed the order as if the petitioner to appear before the fourth respondent on 24.08.2018, admitted their guilt.

On perusal of the counter and on submission made by the learned Additional Government Pleader,
it revealed that there are three accused.
The petitioner is arrayed as A3.
The third respondent inspected the premises of the food safety operator, i.e., retail vendor and had taken samples of Kumaran sambar powder, it was sent for food analysis.
The food analysis report dated 24.03.2017 revealed that the sample was found as mis-branded.

It is contravention of condition under Section 3(1)(zf)
Mr.Sakthivel vs / on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109533351/
2 (c) (I) of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
The adjudicating proceedings are defined under Rule 3.1.1 of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
However, nowhere stated about the furnishing of copies about the charge sheet under Rule 3.1.1(7) of the Rules, copy of analysis report to be served on the accused.
The copy of the report was https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis already sent to the food business operated as contemplated under Rule 2.4.2(6) of the Rules.
Accordingly, the designatory officer must sent one copy of the food safety operator for sample lifted.

In the case on hand, copy of the report was also sent to the manufacturer, ie. the petitioner herein,
addition to retail food operator, where the samples were lifted.
Further, under Rule 3.1.1(8) of the Tules, the adjudication officer should explain the offence alleged to have been committed by them with the rules and regulations.
In the case on hand, the retail vendor alone appeared before the adjudicating officer and the petitioner did not appear, on 17.11.2017.
Subsequently, the petitioner made request on 20.11.2017 that too by way of post, requesting the document which is not permitted under the Rules.
In fact, under Rule 3.1.1(9) of the Rules, the food business operators only to produce documents or evidences relevant to the case before the adjudication officer.
Admittedly, the petitioner being the manufacturer of Kumaran Sambar Power is not entitled for any documents.

That apart, on perusal of the entire records revealed that the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis petitioner had appeared before the fourth respondent on 24.08.2018 and made a statement stating that it was happened on first time and hereafter, it will not be happened and sought for apology and also undertaken not to sell such mis-branded food products.
On recording their statement, the fourth respondent imposed a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- against the petitioner, who is being the manufacturer.
Therefore, this Court finds no infirmity or illegality in the order passed by the fourth respondent and this Petition is liable to be dismissed.
Accordingly, this Writ Petition is dismissed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected Miscellaneous Petitions are closed.
